metaTitle: Using a Canister Stove in Cold Weather
description: Keep a canister stove burning in the cold with the right fuel blend, a warm canister, wind protection and a regulated or remote stove, plus safe warming tips.
directAnswer: Use an isobutane/propane blend, keep the canister warm in a pocket, shield the stove from wind and start on low flame. Below about 15 to 20 degrees F choose a regulated, remote or liquid-fuel stove, and never warm a canister with a flame.
